column1: # The bytes of the protocol of AdHoc Relay for keys given: what a program that speaks it must make of the same keys. One case a
# line: what it is, a tab, of what - spaces between -, a tab, the bytes, hex; and, where a relay answers them, a tab and its answer.
# kid <key>                                       the id of the key, 8 bytes
# bind <key> <id> <address>                       a bind, 24 bytes: of the key, the id of the server - 8 bytes, hex - and the
#                                                 address the relay sees it at
# seen <key> <id> <address>                       what the relay answers a bind made for another address, 12 bytes: the
#                                                 address it sees, and what the key says of it
#                                                 what the relay answers a bind, 17 bytes: the port, the address, its times
#                                                 - how often to knock, seconds; a try of dialing, seconds; how often to bind
#                                                 anew, minutes - and what the key says of them - an answer the key did not
# knock <key> <id> <port> <address>               the key of the knocks of the port, 16 bytes: the knock that opens it
# write <write key> <address>                     a write of a record, 16 bytes
# read <read key> <8 bytes, hex>                  a read of a record, 16 bytes
# answer <read key> <8 bytes> <address> <minutes> what the relay answers that read, 13 bytes: the address, the minutes since
#                                                 it was written, and what the read key says of them
# The answers of the relay are those of one that sees the sender at 127.0.0.1 and has the fixed port 41000 with the key
# Fx2pL8wNq7Rk3mZa, and a record with the write key Wk3vB9xQm5Tz2Lpe and the read key Rk8mP2qLx3Vb7NtY,
# written the minute before, its times as by default - 20 s, 31 s, 30 minutes: a bind made for another address is answered with
# the address, and made again for it.
